next.headline: The flashlight and the camera, in the lock screen's corners.
notes: The lock screen has shortcuts in its bottom corners again: press and hold for the flashlight or the camera, which opens without unlocking. Set each corner to the flashlight, the camera, the QR scanner, Do Not Disturb, an app or nothing under Settings → Lock screen → Shortcuts.
Scan QR codes with Google Lens from a lock-screen shortcut or the new Chronotif QR scanner tile in Quick Settings.

On the lock screen, tapping the top notification opens just that one in place, with a conversation’s messages and its Reply button, instead of unfolding everything. Tap the count under it to see the rest.
Fit to your fingerprint sensor is now under Settings → Lock screen on every phone, for in-screen sensors your phone doesn't tell Chronotif about.
Leaving Settings takes a second Back, so one stray edge swipe doesn't drop you out of it.

stable.headline: The panel comes down under your finger, and the edge handle is yours to shape.
notes: Chronotif now sends anonymous Usage data: counts, panel speeds, settings and crash reports, never anything from your notifications, so it can be improved from how it’s really used. Turn it off under Settings → Privacy and about, where What’s sent lists every field.
The panel opens faster, most of all the first time after an update: the header is there at once and your notifications follow right after.
Swipe down on the status bar and the panel follows your finger, like the system shade. Let go early and it slides back, without counting as a check.
Reopening the panel is quicker: it keeps your cards ready instead of building them again.
Swiping the status bar again right after closing the panel no longer opens the system shade.

The edge handle is easier to hit: a half-circle outline the size of a fingertip, and all of it responds. Pick another shape, style or colour under Settings → Edge handle, including one that doesn't light up for new notifications.
Hold the edge handle and drag it to move it, to either side and any height. Holding it without moving still opens Search, when you let go.
The edge handle steps aside in fullscreen apps.
Settings are split into sections, each with the whole screen to itself, and a menu button slides out a drawer that lists them. Settings reopen where you left them.

Settings have a new look, light or dark as your phone is or as you pick under General, in your wallpaper's colours: settings sit in rounded groups, and choices sit side by side instead of in long lists. General has its on switch at the top, then a checklist of what Chronotif still needs, with a button for each step.

Search settings from the bar at the top: results change with each letter, show where a setting lives and what it's set to, and open its page right at it. The microphone hands the search to your phone's voice input.

After an update, the first time you open the panel it shows what's new since the version you had, and only that: a nightly shows just the lines it added. Your notifications stay New until the sheet is closed.
A Tips page in settings lists the gestures: pulling the panel down, holding a card for its Preview, moving the edge handle, and more.
Tap an open stack's name to close it, as well as Show less.
Snooze a notification from its Preview (press and hold the card) for 15 minutes, an hour, three hours, until tomorrow morning, or until a time you pick. It comes back as new.
The Preview has a Clear button, and Settings → Panel → Swipe to clear lets you stop cards clearing when swiped by accident.
Settings → Search lists what Search can do, with examples to try, below its settings, and the Search tip on the Tips page sums it up.
The lock screen leaves room for the time: the clock stays big, and new notifications wait at the bottom as a pile. Tap it or drag it up to see everything, and press Back to put it away.

While music plays, the lock screen shows the album art large with the player under it, over a blur of the art. Drag up and the art shrinks into the player. Playing music now brings up Chronotif's lock screen on its own.

More works on the lock screen without unlocking: reply right there, use a notification's buttons that don't open the app, see Running, and find contacts and events in Search. Turn on Hide sensitive content to keep contacts and events behind the unlock. Opening an app still asks to unlock.

Double-tap an empty part of the lock screen to turn the screen off, as on your phone's own lock screen. It goes black at once and the phone sleeps a few seconds later. Settings → Lock screen → Double-tap to sleep switches the double tap off.
On the lock screen, tap the clock to open your alarms or the date to open your calendar, as in the panel. Both ask you to unlock first.

On phones with the fingerprint sensor under the screen, Tap to unlock sits on the sensor and the pile above it, so your finger no longer lands on a notification. Settings → Lock screen → Fit to your fingerprint sensor fits it exactly with one touch.
New installs show Chronotif on the lock screen whenever there are notifications, and Search converts currencies without asking first. If you're updating, your settings stay as they were.

Settings → Search starts with a checklist, like General: let Search find contacts and calendar events, place calls and convert currencies, and add its widget to your home screen. Say Not now to any of them; the Search tile is there too if you want it.

Try Chronotif hands-on under Settings → Tutorial: the real panel with made-up notifications, one step at a time. Open it, watch New move to Earlier, open a stack, preview, reply and clear, then open Search every way there is and ask it things, and try the lock screen: the pile, replying while locked, double-tap to sleep. Your own notifications stay hidden and untouched while you practise.
A conversation renamed by its app shows its new name the next time you open the panel, instead of the old one.

stable.headline: Search, from the panel or the lock screen.
notes: Pull down in the panel or the lock-screen view to search. Before you type, it suggests the apps that notified most recently.
Search answers quick math, unit conversions and the time in other cities, opens Android's settings pages, and hands anything else to the web search engine you pick.
Turn on contacts and calendar events under Settings → Search to find people and plans too. While the phone is locked, they stay hidden until you unlock.
Convert currencies with the European Central Bank's daily rates. It's off until you turn it on, and the download carries nothing you type.
Open Search without accessibility: hold the edge handle, or use the Search tile, home-screen widget or app shortcut.
A gear in the panel header opens Android's Settings.

stable.headline: Chats stack by message, and Earlier keeps its order.
notes: A conversation shows one card per message, stacked newest on top, with the person's picture in place of the app icon.
Photos show as thumbnails. Press and hold a message to preview it, and open attachments full screen.
Earlier stays in the order things arrived. One app's cards that arrived close together fold into a stack.
The panel header shows the time and date. Tap the clock to open your clock app.
Paused media players can be swiped away when the app allows it. Contributed by lgg.
Update checks read GitHub's release pages, so they no longer hit a rate limit.

stable.headline: The panel opens over your apps.
notes: The panel opens as an overlay, so the app underneath keeps running.
Swipe down on the left half of the status bar to open Chronotif. It's optional and uses an accessibility service.
Tap empty space to close the panel, if you turn it on. Contributed by lgg.
The lock-screen view no longer dims your wallpaper.
Setup warns when notification access is on but Chronotif has lost its connection.

stable.headline: A media player, a Running group, and Stable or Nightly updates.
notes: Music and video notifications show as a player with artwork, controls and a seek bar.
Always-running items, like step counters and downloads, fold into a Running group below the list.
Choose Stable or Nightly under Settings → Updates.
A switch turns Chronotif on and off.
A New chat card lists every message since your last check.
The lock-screen view sleeps after the lock screen's own short timeout.
Cards stay readable in dark mode when an app sets its own text colours.

stable.headline: A quicker lock-screen view.
notes: The lock-screen view steps aside after 10 seconds untouched, like the stock lock screen.
Tap outside a card to start unlocking.
The Quick Settings tile is now called Chronotif.

stable.headline: A fix for Android 16.
notes: Fixes a crash on start on Android 16 when automatic updates are on.

stable.headline: Updates from GitHub.
notes: Turn on automatic updates and Chronotif checks GitHub once a day, verifies the new APK against its checksum and installs it. Check for updates does the same on demand.
Signed with Chronotif's permanent key. Coming from 0.1.0, uninstall it once first.

stable.headline: The first release.
notes: A notification panel and a lock-screen view, newest first, split into New and Earlier at your last check.
Open the panel from the edge handle or the Quick Settings tile.
